claims.text: At stage-3 DonHang.Api holds two modules, Ordering and Catalog (Catalog reached only through ICatalog), while Notifications and Payments run as separate services: a modular monolith with two services split off.

An architecture style is good or bad only against a set of drivers; the same team can rightly reach different styles for different systems or at different times, and a changed driver, not fashion, is the reason to revisit.
In ADR 0003 the in-API option is rejected because the gateway's key and the money rows would not sit in a service of their own; no option is rejected for YC-7 or YC-9.
No ADR in docs/adr/ at stage-3 (0001-0010) splits Catalog out or names a driver that would require it; Catalog stays a module.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docs/adr/ listing; STAGE.md lines 10-13

claims.text: Recording the drivers in the ADR, not only the chosen style, lets a team see which choices rested on a driver when it changes and weigh them again.

ADR 0003 context (lines 13-17): accept a refund within 2 s even if the gateway fails (YC-7), never refund twice (YC-9), keep resending for at least 24 h before staff take over (YC-10); the key and money rows are the most sensitive part; in version 1 every DonHang.Api copy holds the key.
ADR 0003's context names no style; the separate service appears only in its options and decision, as the option keeping the key and money rows in a service of their own.

ADR 0002 lines 12-21: at stage-2 email rows are written in the order's transaction and sent by every DonHang.Api copy; that was right for one process; two things changed: Payments must also message customers, and a slow or failing email server takes resources from order taking.
ADR 0002 lines 23-24 reject the number of copies as a reason: the email job could run with the API's number of copies.

Trade-offs table: in one process every copy holds the gateway key and a slow email server slows order taking; with services only Payments holds the key, orders are still placed while Notifications is down (messages wait in the queue), and each service adds an image, pipeline, database and dashboard.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0003 @ stage-3 lines 16-17, 24-26, 42; docs/adr/0002 lines 20-21, 31-34, 43 (consequences section, from line 41)

claims.text: No style wins every column; which driver counts differs per part: the key decided Payments, email failure isolation together with Payments messaging customers decided Notifications, and nothing asked to split Catalog.
claims.source_hint: Reading of ADRs 0002, 0003 @ stage-3; outline item 5

claims.text: If more copies of the whole process carry the load, scaling alone does not justify a service; two teams that deploy one process share every release and may wait on each other, a driver worth weighing a split for; a small new system with one developer fits one process with layers.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0002 @ stage-3 lines 23-24; docs/adr/0012 @ stage-4 lines 56-57 (teams waiting on each other); design.l3.when-to-extract-a-service summary lines 1-2

claims.text: Microservices are not a target or a level of maturity; a style that suits many teams and heavy load answers those drivers, and copying it brings its costs without the needs that pay for them.

ADR 0003 lists refunds inside DonHang.Api and refunds in a separate service as options, so the feature alone did not decide the shape; a late non-functional requirement such as answering while a dependency fails can force work out of a request, a structural change.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0003 @ stage-3 lines 21-26; management.l2.non-functional-requirements summary line 5
